title: Discourse grammar
note: cohesion beyond linkers · demonstrative reference with this / these / such a, agreeing in number with a clause-sized referent · summary (shell) nouns packaging the preceding text and judging it · topic-announcing frames as for, turning to, with regard to, when it comes to, in terms of, as far as … is concerned · parallel reference across the former, the latter, the same applies / is true of / goes for, likewise, respectively · 4 strands x 12 · 48 items · built to live 2026-08-07 (cloud run 15)

items.en: The client changed the plan again. This is now a serious problem.
items.cz: Klient znovu změnil plán. To je teď vážný problém.
items.gap: The client changed the plan again. ____ is now a serious problem.
accepts: The client changed the plan again. This is now a serious problem.
items.explanation: English points back at what it has just said with this, these and such, and the choice is grammar, not decoration. This and these reach back over a whole clause — not to a noun in it, but to the fact the clause reported — and they must agree in number with what they stand for: one event is this, several are these. Such is different again: it points not at the thing itself but at its kind, and before a singular countable noun it takes a: such a delay, never this a delay. Czech carries all of this on one word, to, which is why Czech writers reach for it in English and produce a sentence that floats free of the paragraph above it.
items.explanation_cz: Angličtina odkazuje na to, co právě řekla, slovy this, these a such, a ta volba je věcí gramatiky, nikoli ozdoby. This a these sahají zpět přes celou větu — ne k některému jejímu jménu, nýbrž k faktu, který věta oznámila — a musí se shodovat v čísle s tím, co zastupují: jedna událost je this, několik jich je these. Such je ještě něco jiného: neukazuje na věc samu, ale na její druh, a před počitatelným jménem v jednotném čísle bere a: such a delay, nikdy this a delay. Čeština tohle všechno unese na jediném slově to, a proto po něm čeští pisatelé v angličtině sahají a vzniká věta, která se vznáší bez vazby na odstavec nad sebou.

items.explanation: Instead of pointing back with a bare this, careful English writing packages the preceding text inside a noun: this decision, that assumption, this delay. The noun does two jobs at once. It ties the sentence to what came before, and it tells the reader how to file what came before — calling a statement an assumption already judges it, and calling it a claim judges it differently. These summary nouns are the backbone of academic and business prose, and choosing the wrong one is not a style slip but a change of meaning. A bare this is always available and always weaker; the noun is what makes the link say something.
items.explanation_cz: Místo holého this pečlivá angličtina předchozí text zabalí do podstatného jména: this decision, that assumption, this delay. To jméno dělá dvě věci najednou. Váže větu k tomu, co bylo řečeno dřív, a zároveň čtenáři říká, jak si to má zařadit — nazvat výrok předpokladem už znamená jej hodnotit a nazvat jej tvrzením znamená hodnotit jej jinak. Tato shrnující jména jsou páteří odborné i obchodní prózy a špatná volba není stylistickým přehmatem, nýbrž změnou významu. Holé this je vždycky po ruce a vždycky slabší; teprve jméno dá odkazu obsah.

Alongside them sits the same, which carries a whole statement across to a new subject — the same applies to, the same is true of, the same goes for — and likewise, which does the same work as a sentence adverb. All of these depend on the reader holding the earlier pair in mind, so they belong in writing that is close-knit; used at a distance they simply lose the reader, and the honest repair is to name the thing again.

cards.title: Cohesion is grammar
cards.body: A paragraph is not a list of correct sentences. Each sentence has to reach back and take hold of the one before it, and English does that reaching with grammar: with the words it chooses to point back, with the nouns it uses to package what has been said, and with the phrases it puts in front of a sentence to announce what it is now about. Linkers such as however and although are only the visible part of this. The rest is what separates prose that holds together from prose that is merely accurate.
cards.body_cz: Odstavec není seznam správných vět. Každá věta se musí ohlédnout a chytit se té předchozí, a angličtina se ohlíží gramatikou: slovy, jimiž odkazuje zpět, jmény, do nichž balí to, co už bylo řečeno, a frázemi, které staví před větu, aby ohlásila, o čem teď bude. Spojovací výrazy jako however a although jsou jen viditelnou částí toho všeho. Zbytek je to, co odlišuje text, který drží pohromadě, od textu, který je pouze správný.

table.caption: four ways a sentence holds on to the one before
rows: The system stopped twice. This has never been the case before.
The board voted to close the office. This decision…
As for the budget, nothing has changed.
The former is cheaper; the latter is safer.

cards.title: this and these point at facts
cards.title_cz: this a these ukazují na fakta
cards.body: This and these do not reach back to a noun in the previous sentence — they reach back to the whole thing it said. That is why they can begin a sentence with no noun after them at all. They must agree in number with what they stand for: one event or one fact is this, two or more are these. Czech does the whole job with to, and a Czech writer who translates to as it produces an English sentence that has come loose from the paragraph above it.
cards.body_cz: This a these se nevracejí k některému jménu v předchozí větě — vracejí se k tomu, co celá věta řekla. Proto mohou stát na začátku věty i bez jakéhokoli jména za sebou. Musejí se shodovat v čísle s tím, co zastupují: jedna událost či jeden fakt je this, dvě a více jich je these. Čeština si vystačí se slovem to, a český pisatel, který to přeloží jako it, vytvoří anglickou větu, jež se odpoutala od odstavce nad sebou.

table.caption: number follows the referent, not the last noun
rows: The system stopped twice on Monday.
This has never been the case before.
Prices went up and sales fell.
These changes have hurt the team.
The report was late and the figures were wrong.

points: The verb gives the number away: this is · these are. Read it back and the wrong one is audible.
Such points at the kind, not the thing, and takes a before a singular noun: such a delay.
Never this a delay or these a delay — a belongs to such alone.

cards.title: Package it in a noun
cards.body: A bare this is always available and always the weakest option. Careful writing puts a noun after it, and that noun does a second job on top of the linking: it tells the reader how to classify what was just said. Calling a statement an assumption already casts doubt on it; calling the same statement a claim casts a different kind of doubt; calling it a decision does not question it at all. Choosing the noun is choosing the reading.
cards.body_cz: Holé this je vždycky po ruce a vždycky je nejslabší volbou. Pečlivý text za ně postaví podstatné jméno a to jméno kromě navázání dělá ještě druhou věc: říká čtenáři, jak si má právě řečené zařadit. Nazvat výrok předpokladem už znamená jej zpochybnit; nazvat týž výrok tvrzením jej zpochybní jinak; nazvat jej rozhodnutím jej nezpochybní vůbec. Volba jména je volbou výkladu.

table.caption: the noun is the judgement
rows: He said the data were complete.
taken for granted, may be false
He argued that the market will grow.
The board voted to close the office.
The parts arrived three weeks late.
names the event as a problem

points: The noun must genuinely cover what came before — a vote is a decision, not a question.
This success and this failure both name a result; they are not interchangeable with each other.
In writing, prefer the noun. This alone is fine in speech and thin on the page.

cards.title: Announce the topic first
cards.body: English tells the reader what a sentence is about before telling them anything about it. When the subject changes, a short phrase goes in front, names the new topic, and is closed off with a comma. These are fixed frames: the small words inside them cannot be swapped for near neighbours, and getting one wrong is the commonest way an otherwise good C1 sentence sounds translated.
cards.body_cz: Angličtina čtenáři řekne, o čem věta je, dřív než mu o tom řekne cokoli dalšího. Když se mění téma, postaví se dopředu krátká fráze, pojmenuje nové téma a oddělí se čárkou. Jsou to pevné rámce: drobná slova uvnitř nich nelze zaměnit za blízké sousedy a právě chyba v nich je nejčastějším důvodem, proč jinak dobrá věta na úrovni C1 zní jako překlad.

table.caption: fixed frames — the small words are not free
rows: As for the budget, the plan has not changed.
Turning to costs, the picture is worse.
With regard to the meeting, I have no news.
When it comes to price, we are the cheapest.
In terms of speed, the new system is better.
As far as the deadline is concerned, we are safe.

points: Turning to is a participle and only works in that form: not Turned to costs.
As far as needs both halves — as far as X is concerned. Dropping is concerned leaves it unfinished.
All of them take a comma before the main clause.

cards.title: former, latter, the same
cards.body: Once two things have been named, English can pick either up again without repeating it. The former is the first of the two and the latter the second, and they work only when there are exactly two. The same carries a whole statement over to a new subject, and likewise does the same job as a sentence adverb. Respectively pairs off two later items with two earlier ones in the order they were given — it is not a general-purpose also.
cards.body_cz: Jakmile byly dvě věci pojmenovány, může se k nim angličtina vrátit, aniž by je opakovala. The former je první z těch dvou a the latter druhá; fungují jen tehdy, jsou-li právě dvě. The same přenáší celé tvrzení na nový podmět a likewise dělá totéž jako větné příslovce. Respectively přiřadí dvě pozdější položky ke dvěma dřívějším v pořadí, v jakém byly uvedeny — není to univerzální „také“.

table.caption: picking a pair back up
rows: The same applies to small companies.
The same is true of Prague.
The same goes for the Brno team.
Likewise, the Brno team was late.
The offices opened in 1994 and 2018 respectively.

points: Former and latter need exactly two items — with three, name them.
The same is a noun phrase here: the same applies, never same applies.
Respectively goes at the end and only ever pairs two ordered lists.

cards.title: When the link fails
cards.body: Every device on these cards depends on the reader being able to find what it points at, immediately and without a second guess. If two candidates are in play, if the referent is a paragraph away, or if a bare this is carrying more than one idea at once, the link fails silently — the sentence still parses, and the reader simply loses the thread. The repair is never a better pointing word; it is a noun, or the thing named again in full.
cards.body_cz: Každý prostředek z těchto karet stojí na tom, že čtenář okamžitě a bez váhání najde, k čemu odkazuje. Jsou-li ve hře dva možné odkazované členy, leží-li odkazovaný člen o odstavec výš, nebo nese-li holé this víc než jednu myšlenku najednou, odkaz tiše selže — věta se pořád dá rozebrat a čtenář jen ztratí nit. Opravou nikdy není lepší odkazovací slovo, nýbrž podstatné jméno nebo věc pojmenovaná znovu a celá.

table.caption: diagnose it by asking what exactly?
rows: The manager told the client this was wrong.
two people, and this has no clear referent
Prices rose, staff left and the office closed. This was serious.
The former is cheaper, the latter is safer, the third is faster.
former and latter cover two, not three
As for that, we have no news.
that names no topic — the frame needs a noun

points: Ask what exactly? after every this. If you cannot answer in one noun, write the noun in.
Across a paragraph break, name the thing again — the reader has let go of it.
In formal writing the fuller version is never wrong, only heavier.
